name: move_pose
description:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public TCP to a stated position and orientation. This surface drives one right arm: send the target fields directly, with no targets wrapper and no arm choice. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta, world_axes) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in the arguments themselves. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; world_axes takes approach_world and jaw_line_world; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name. speed (optional) is fast, normal or careful. fast is the default and the normal choice. normal (about 0.3 m/s and 60 deg/s) is for moves near objects, and while holding an object (fast's hard accelerations can make it slip). careful (about 0.1 m/s and 20 deg/s) is for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing; for that last bit, slow_approaching: true (fast or normal) slows only the final 2 cm of the same move to careful and is preferred over a whole careful move; use it when placing a held object. Slower speeds use more control ticks and native actions, so use them only where they help. These are guidance, not enforced. Instead of speed you may give speed_m_s, any number above 0: the top speed of the grip site in m/s, with a turn-rate cap of 200 deg/s per m/s (at least 20 deg/s), both reached in 0.25 s. Whatever the speed, each joint's own speed is the real ceiling (at most 57.3 deg/s on this arm for free_space, 28.6 for precision and 13.8 for contact_approach, at every speed): where a hand move needs large joint turns, or for a high speed_m_s, the arm moves slower than asked, so a fast request may not be reached; a slow one practically always is. last_action_effect.detail.motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says the top speed the plan reaches.
Effect: compiles the request once. Every interaction runs on the arm's joint-position controller along a joint path that admission computes and checks before any motion. free_space takes a global route, planned from the measured joints around the collision world described below. precision moves the grip site along the straight line to the target, solved by inverse kinematics every 20 mm, unless it turns the hand more than 15 degrees, when it takes the global route as free_space does; contact_approach always moves along the straight line. On each 50 ms control tick the joint targets advance along that path by at most 2.86 deg, 1.43 deg or 0.688 deg per joint and move the grip site at most 30 mm and 8.59 deg, 12 mm and 4.58 deg, or 8 mm and 3.44 deg (free_space, precision, contact_approach). The arm has arrived once the measured joints stay within 0.286 deg of the path's end for 3 consecutive ticks and the measured grip site is then within 5 mm and 2.86 deg of the target; otherwise the action ends as not_reached with failure_code endpoint_residual_exceeded. contact_approach ends early, as reached with endpoint.stop_reason contact_detected, once the measured gripper contact force reaches 15 N. Measured joints trailing their targets by more than 11.46 deg for 3 consecutive ticks (endpoint.stop_reason joint_lag), coming to rest short of the path's end once the last target was sent (every joint moving less than 0.0573 deg a tick for 3 consecutive ticks: settle_stalled), or still unsettled 20 ticks after the last target was sent (settle_timeout), mean the arm is held back by something: the action ends as not_reached with failure_code blocked (as reached if the grip site is on target anyway) and the arm holds where it stopped; stop_evidence names the joint farthest from its target. An action still moving after 150 ticks (7.5 s) ends as not_reached with failure_code controller_timeout. Every control tick spends one native action. A target more than 1.05 m from the arm's shoulder at the current base pose, at the nearest shoulder height the torso lift allows, is rejected before any motion (plan_rejected, target_out_of_reach_from_base; admission_refusal gives distance_from_mount_m, reach_m and nearest_mount_height_m); move the base closer first. Global routes and every line avoid a collision world rebuilt for each request from the current depth images of both cameras: the robot arm removed, a held object moving with the hand, the space around the goal hand cleared (contact at the goal is not checked), and space no camera sees, such as behind objects or under the base, counted as free. A global route must find a path clear of that world. A straight line must solve at every cut, with no joint jumping more than 14.3 deg between cuts, and keep the arm's links out of that world, within 10 mm, along the whole line; a precision line keeps the gripper and a held object out too, while contact_approach may press them against anything. A refusal's admission_refusal says, for a line, how far along it failed (path_fraction) and which robot part enters the world (robot_part: arm or gripper), or, where its inverse kinematics stopped, why (cause: ik_unsolved, or joint_branch_jump with the joint and its jump_deg against bound_deg), the cut's pose (at_pose) and whether the target itself is reachable from here (endpoint: reachable, reachable_only_through_the_world or unreachable; reachable means the line, not the target, is what fails); a global route that finds no path says neither, and its planner's own sentence, where it has one, ends the summary. The gripper or a held object running into a fixture on the way needs an approach from the open side first: move to a pose in front of or above the opening, then in. The arm entering the world means this base pose cannot reach the target: move the base closer or turn it. When the arm alone cannot reach the target at the current torso height, the lift is admitted at the nearest height, tried every 0.04 m of the lift's 0.34 m of travel, from which the whole move is: the path from there (the line's inverse kinematics, joint jumps and world check, or the global route) in the current depth images as seen from there, then its timing and wrist check at the requested speed, as the real call checks them; a straight line whose target the arm reaches from here does not lift. The torso moves there first with the arm held, at most 0.05 m per control tick and at most 30 ticks (counted as native actions), stays there afterwards, and the effect reports it under torso (from_m, to_m, target_m; torso_height_m in public_robot_facts.mobile_base). The path is then planned again from where the lift stopped, in the world seen from there: if none exists then, the action ends as not_reached with the same failure codes and the torso stays where it went. A target that does not solve within 5 mm and 2.86 deg at any torso height, or whose path would enter the world, is rejected before any motion (plan_rejected with target_unreachable_at_base_pose, target_in_collision_at_base_pose or path_in_collision_at_base_pose; motion_planner_unavailable when the planner itself failed, which says nothing about the target) and spends no native action. Move the base or choose another orientation. A refusal with target_out_of_reach_from_base, target_unreachable_at_base_pose, target_in_collision_at_base_pose or path_in_collision_at_base_pose carries admission_refusal.base_suggestions, nearest first, at most two, and the summary names the first: base poses within base_search.max_travel_m of the base from which this same move is admitted, each a ready move_base target (x_m, y_m, yaw_deg) with distance_m and turn_deg from here, at the current torso height. Each was checked on the current depth images only, as seen from there, the way this call is checked: the same path (the straight line or the global route) in that world, then its timing and wrist check at this speed (arm_path admitted); inverse kinematics also reaches the target wherever move_base may stop within its arrival tolerance; the floor under the base there was seen; and along the move there neither the base's footprint nor the arm, carried at its joints, meets what the images show. An empty list means none was found (base_search counts what was asked, arm_blocked those the carried arm would meet the depth on the way to: retract the arm first); a line whose target is reachable from here, or whose gripper is what enters the world, gets none. move_pose itself never moves the base: move_base there first, and the next move_pose lifts the torso only if it must. The speed holds on every arm move; move_base keeps its own speeds. The admitted path is timed so the grip site keeps the speed's caps, one joint target per 50 ms control tick (fast: no Cartesian speed limit, the joints alone), within the per-tick advance above at every speed. Before anything moves, the path is refused (plan_rejected, with no controller write and no native action spent) when its grip site would turn more than 45 degrees beyond the turn from its start to its planned end orientation (paced_path_wrist_unwind: the wrist would unwind the long way round, typically at its last joint's limit. Other paths to the same pose are tried first, and with open jaws the move runs at its jaw twin instead, the orientation turned a half-turn about the approach axis, which grips the same: last_action_effect.detail.motion.wrist.jaw_flip_retry then says so and arrival is judged at the twin. Refused anyway, or while the jaws hold something, ask for a target orientation nearer the current one) or when it needs more than 130 control ticks at the requested speed (paced_motion_budget: use a faster speed or split the move); last_action_effect.detail.motion.refused gives the numbers. A move is never cut part way, so it never stops in the middle of a wrist turn.
Returns: an immediate acknowledgement with status=submitted, action and compiled_pose; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The later receipt separates refusal, arrival and recoverable non-arrival, and available contact feedback includes requested versus measured motion, force/progress evidence and truthful unknown values. The subsequent Supervisor receipt and fresh causal observation separately report execution route, phase outcomes and measured residuals. The later receipt's last_action_effect.detail.motion reports speed (speed -- custom with speed_m_s -- speed_m_s when given, slow_approaching, the caps linear_m_s, angular_deg_s and joint_speed_deg_s, and planned_peak_linear_m_s and planned_peak_angular_deg_s: the top speed and turn rate the planned path reaches under every cap, joints included; with slow_approaching also slow_approach_m and the slow caps), wrist (the last wrist joint from the measured joints through every planned control tick: start_deg, end_deg, min_deg, max_deg, travel_deg and min_limit_margin_deg to its joint limit, since the two ends alone can hide a swing; and the grip site's path_turn_deg and requested_turn_deg), planned_ticks and duration_s. A pre-admission error submits no action.
Does not: avoid what the depth images do not show; change an exact requested orientation; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; retry a failed motion.
On error: Refused: an unknown field, a mode without its companion fields or a field of another mode, each naming the field; hold_current for both halves, a target equal to the measured pose, a rotation_angle_deg outside [-180, 180] or an orientation_xyzw whose norm lies outside [0.98, 1.02], each as invalid_motion_arguments without a field; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the grip site is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Also refused as invalid_motion_arguments naming the field: a speed other than fast, normal or careful; a speed_m_s that is not a number above 0 or comes with a speed; slow_approaching with speed careful or with speed_m_s at or below 0.1 (it has no effect there). position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. plan_rejected means zero controller writes; not_reached means execution started but the arm did not arrive (failure_code blocked, endpoint_residual_exceeded, controller_timeout or episode_terminal_during_execution). Use the named phase and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance (also on move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch): the jaw footprint's lowest point at the target (fingers, plus the held object's localized extent when the jaws hold a named target) minus the highest surface the current depth images show beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher; occluded surfaces are unknown; not a collision check. The jaws count as holding when the last gripper command was close and the measured jaw separation exceeds 3 mm, which does not confirm a grasp. world_axes compiles approach_world (the grip site's local +Z) and jaw_line_world (its local +X) into orientation_xyzw. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.target_axes_world, on move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch, gives the submitted orientation's world approach and jaw-line directions. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance.claim_boundary (move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch) is "From the current depth images and their calibration only; points inside the measured jaws, the held object and the space above them are excluded as robot, other robot links are not; occluded surfaces and object undersides are unknown; points up to the footprint's top within radius_m count; not a collision check or a contact prediction, and the move is submitted unchanged.".

inputSchema.description: This surface drives one right arm, so the arguments are that arm's target with no targets wrapper and no arm choice.

position_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no position fields; absolute REQUIRES position_m; delta REQUIRES translation_m AND position_frame. A mode alone supplies no values.

position_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=absolute. [x,y,z] in world metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

translation_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with position_frame. [dx,dy,dz] in metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

position_frame.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with translation_m. world uses fixed world axes; end_effector uses current controlled-frame axes. Never inferred. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no orientation fields; absolute_quaternion REQUIRES orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta REQUIRES rotation_axis AND rotation_angle_deg AND orientation_frame; world_axes REQUIRES approach_world AND jaw_line_world. A mode alone supplies no values.

orientation_xyzw.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion. Unit quaternion [x,y,z,w]. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_axis.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_angle_deg, orientation_frame. An x, y or z axis in orientation_frame. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_angle_deg.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, orientation_frame. Signed DEGREES, not radians. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_frame.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg. world or current end_effector axes. Never inferred. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

approach_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with jaw_line_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the approach axis. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

jaw_line_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with approach_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the jaw line, made perpendicular to approach_world. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

interaction.description: Physical intent, never a controller name. Omitted means free_space. Null means omitted.

speed.description: Optional; default fast (the normal choice). normal: about 0.3 m/s, for moves near objects and while holding an object. careful: about 0.1 m/s, for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing. Slower speeds use more control ticks and native actions. Leave it out when you give speed_m_s. Null means omitted.

speed_m_s.description: Optional, instead of speed: the top speed of the grip site in m/s, any number above 0 (turn rate capped at 200 deg/s per m/s, at least 20 deg/s). Each joint's own speed (at most 57.3 deg/s on this arm for free_space, 28.6 for precision and 13.8 for contact_approach) stays the ceiling, so a high value may not be reached; last_action_effect.detail.motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says what the plan reaches. Slower speeds use more control ticks and native actions. Null means omitted.

slow_approaching.description: Optional; default false. true slows only the last 2 cm of the path to the careful speed inside the same move (with speed fast or normal, or speed_m_s above 0.1; refused with careful). Preferred over a whole careful move for the end of an approach, contact or placing. Null means omitted.

observed_clearance.description: Read-only, from the current depth images: the jaw footprint's lowest point at this target minus the highest observed surface beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher. Not a collision check.

held_object.description: null unless the jaws measure as holding: the target the policy named when they closed and whether its localized extent is part of the footprint.
null unless the jaws measure as holding: the target the policy named when they closed and whether its localized extent is part of the footprint.

target_axes_world.description: World directions of the approach axis and jaw line of the submitted target orientation, computed from its compiled quaternion.
